course.title: Mobile App Development for Data Science (Android & ML Integration)
course.description: Mobile Application Development provides hands-on training in building Android applications using Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. The course begins with core mobile concepts and the Android ecosystem, then progresses to Kotlin programming foundations and Android project structure. Students develop modern declarative UIs with Compose, including layouts, Material components, input handling, lists, and user feedback patterns. They learn essential Compose concepts such as composition/recomposition, state hoisting, and state management, and implement navigation for multi-screen apps. The course then focuses on integrating RESTful APIs using Retrofit and OkHttp, mapping JSON to Kotlin data classes, using coroutines for asynchronous calls, and presenting network results with loading/error/retry UI patterns and a recommended repository approach. In the final part, students are introduced to machine learning for mobile developers and implement on-device intelligence using TensorFlow Lite concepts and ML Kit capabilities (such as OCR/barcode scanning), including performance considerations and responsible AI practices (privacy, consent, and bias awareness). By the end, students can build complete Android apps that combine UI, networking, and practical ML-powered features.

topics.title: Topic 1: Introduction to Mobile Application Development
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Define mobile applications and describe key characteristics of mobile environments (mobility, constraints, user context). LLO2: Differentiate native, cross-platform, and hybrid apps with examples and suitable use cases. LLO3: Identify common mobile app categories (utility, social, e-commerce, education) and their core features. LLO4: Compare mobile apps vs web apps in terms of performance, offline capability, and device feature access.

topics.title: Topic 2: Introduction to Android App Development
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe the Android ecosystem (Android Studio, SDK, Gradle, Jetpack) and how they work together. LLO2: Create and run a new Android project using a Jetpack Compose template. LLO3: Identify key parts of an Android project structure (app module, manifest, Gradle scripts, resources). LLO4: Explain core Android app components (Activity, Intent, Service, BroadcastReceiver) at a conceptual level. LLO5: Explain the purpose of the Activity lifecycle and why lifecycle awareness matters. LLO6: Deploy and test an app on an emulator and a physical Android device.

topics.title: Topic 3: Introduction to Kotlin
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Use Kotlin syntax correctly (val/var, type inference, string templates). LLO2: Implement control flow using if/else, when, loops, and ranges. LLO3: Write functions with default/named parameters and use lambdas effectively. LLO4: Manipulate collections (List/Set/Map) using map/filter/forEach operations. LLO5: Create Kotlin classes with constructors, properties, and methods using basic OOP principles. LLO6: Apply Kotlin best practices for clean and readable code (naming, immutability, reuse).

topics.title: Topic 4: Implement on Compose
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain the declarative UI concept and how Compose differs from imperative UI approaches. LLO2: Create composable functions, use previews, and apply modifiers (padding, size, click, alignment). LLO3: Build UI layouts using Column, Row, Box, and organize UI into reusable components. LLO4: Implement Material 3 UI components (Text, Button, Card, Scaffold, TopAppBar, Icon). LLO5: Handle user input with TextField, apply basic validation, and display user feedback (Snackbar/Dialog). LLO6: Build scrolling lists using LazyColumn/LazyRow and display images/resources correctly. LLO7: Apply state concepts: composition/recomposition, state hoisting, stateful vs stateless composables. LLO8: Implement state management using remember/rememberSaveable and introduce ViewModel separation. LLO9: Create multi-screen apps using Compose Navigation, routes, arguments, and back stack behavior.

topics.title: Topic 5: Networking and API Integration
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain REST API basics (endpoints, HTTP methods, status codes) and how mobile apps consume APIs. LLO2: Map JSON responses into Kotlin data classes for use in the app. LLO3: Implement API calls using Retrofit interfaces and annotations. LLO4: Configure OkHttp logging and apply debugging techniques for networking issues. LLO5: Perform asynchronous networking using Kotlin coroutines. LLO6: Implement error-handling patterns (timeout, no internet, API error responses). LLO7: Display network results using UI states (Loading/Success/Error) with retry behavior. LLO8: Apply a simple Repository approach to separate networking logic from UI code.

topics.title: Topic 6: Introduction to Machine Learning for Mobile Developers
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain machine learning concepts and distinguish ML from traditional programming. LLO2: Define key ML terms: dataset, features, labels, training, inference. LLO3: Identify mobile ML task types (classification, OCR, detection, recommendation) and suitable use cases. LLO4: Compare on-device ML vs cloud ML in terms of privacy, latency, offline access, and cost. LLO5: Describe mobile ML constraints (model size, speed, battery, memory) and their impact on apps. LLO6: Explain responsible AI concerns in mobile apps (privacy, consent, bias awareness).

topics.title: Topic 7: TensorFlow Lite Fundamentals
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Explain what TensorFlow Lite is and why it is used for on-device inference. LLO2: Describe the inference pipeline (input → preprocessing → inference → output decoding). LLO3: Identify model input requirements (shape, size, normalization) and common data preparation steps. LLO4: Interpret output predictions (top-k classes, confidence scores) and describe limitations. LLO5: Explain optimization concepts such as quantization and the trade-off between speed and accuracy. LLO6: Diagnose common integration issues (wrong input shape, label mismatch, slow inference).

topics.title: Topic 8: ML Kit Integration for On-Device Intelligence
topics.llosRaw: LLO1: Describe ML Kit capabilities and select an appropriate feature (OCR/barcode/face detection optional). LLO2: Implement required permissions and apply privacy considerations for camera/gallery inputs. LLO3: Process images from camera or gallery and display ML results in a Compose UI. LLO4: Implement real-time processing basics (camera frames) and apply performance-friendly strategies. LLO5: Handle edge cases (low light, blur, no result, permission denied) with user-friendly UI behavior. LLO6: Integrate ML output into app workflow (OCR → fill form fields, barcode → fetch API data). LLO7: (Optional) Store recognition history locally and show results in a list UI.

studentResponsibilitiesRaw: Read the learning materials beforehand which means to be ready for the next session. Be completely engaged in class, active, take notes, and ask questions in class. Students are required to participate in various activities in and out of the classroom, such as group work, and individual homework for assignments and reports assigned by the subject teacher. Submit the assigned tasks such as homework, assignments, or research proposal on time.
coursePolicyRaw: Attendance & Preparation Students are expected to attend all classes (online/on-site). Assigned readings and preparation outlines must be completed before class if any. Active participation in group discussions and post-chapter evaluations is required. Academic Integrity All assignments, quizzes, and exams must be done individually. Academic misconduct includes: - Presenting others’ work as one’s own. - Engaging in plagiarism or cheating. Homework & Assignments Preparation outlines must be submitted on time; late submissions incur penalties. Peer discussion is encouraged, but midterm and final exams must be independent. Examinations Midterm and final exams are closed-book. Penalties Violations of academic integrity may result in a failing grade and referral to the Office of Student Affairs. Students uncertain about potential violations should consult the instructor in advance.
